text.p: Pen pictures of the AC Milan players most likely to appear in Sunday's serie A clash with Juventus.

Sebastiano Rossi, goalkeeper, 32. First choice keeper since 1992 but fans blame him for Milan's poor defensive record this season. One of best in serie A and only churlish attitude toward opponents and team-mates has denied him international honours. Unbeaten for record 929 minutes in serie A in 1994/95.

Paolo Maldini, defender, 28. Son of Under-21 coach Cesare, Maldini has been fixture in Milan since debut at age of 16 in 1985. Reputation as best-attacking full-back in world undermined by poor form for Italy at Euro 96 and, more recently, for Milan. Italy captain. Disc jockey for Milan radio station.

Christian Panucci, defender, 23. Signed from Genoa in 1993, tender age belies experience, including key role in Milan's 1994 European Cup triumph over Barcelona and two Under-21 European titles. Good going forward, suspect in defence. Narrowly escaped boarding doomed TWA flight 103 in New York in the summer.

Franco Baresi, defender, 36. Milan's longest-serving player in his final season. Symbol of club's transformation under Silvio Berlusconi, lifting three European Cups and five league titles in 10 years. Niggling ankle injury has limited "Kaiser Franz" to one league match this season.

Alessandro Costacurta, defender, 30. Another product of Milan youth team. Good man-to-man marker but has suffered absence of Baresi more than any other player, losing form and place in national side. In 1994, yellow cards cost him place in World and European Cup finals.

Marcel Desailly, defender, 28. With Marseille side that defeated Milan in 1993 European Cup final. At Milan six months later, where, at Baresi's request, filled holding role between midfield and defence. Nicknamed "The Rock", Desailly is now filling the central defensive role he holds in French side.

Demetrio Albertini, midfielder, 25. Reared in Milan youth team but farmed out to Padua for season before earning first-team place in 1991. Playmaker in Milan and national side. Packs powerful shot. Penalty-taker. First league goal versus Juventus in 1991. Committed Catholic whose brother is a priest.

Zvonimir Boban, midfielder, 28. Started with Dynamo Zagreb. Signed for Milan in 1991 but lent to Bari for season. Gifted passer who likes to get into goal-scoring positions. Croatia captain. National hero after protecting fans from truncheon-welding police in last Yugoslav Cup final. Keen chess player.

Edgar Davids, midfielder, 23. Signed from Ajax after impressing Milan with versatile performance in 1995 European Cup win. Quickly won first-team place but still to conquer feisty temperament. Broke wrist in Milan street punch-up.

Stefano Eranio, midfielder, 29. Started career with home-town Genoa, reaching 1992 UEFA Cup semi-finals before joining Milan. Aggressive midfielder with fierce shot. Italian international who only missed 1994 World Cup finals because of knee injury.

Tomas Locatelli, midfielder, 20. Heralded as "Milan's answer to Alessandro Del Piero" after being signed from Atalanta in 1995. But looks more like ready-made replacement for departed Roberto Donadoni, allying tactical discipline to talent. Scored winner against IFK Gothenburg in Champions' League.

Dejan Savicevic, midfielder, 30. Montenegrin signed from Red Star Belgrade in 1992. Fell out with coach Fabio Capello and only took first-team place after Berlusconi intervened. Nicknamed "The Genie" for ability to conjure up openings. Troublesome hamstring has kept him out for most of season.

George Weah, striker, 30. Last year's World, European and African player of the year. Spent six seasons in France before moving to Milan last season. Now considered the natural replacement for Dutchman Marco Van Basten. Liberian, capable of turning defeat into victory with inspired moments of skill.

Cristophe Dugarry, striker, 24. French international signed from Bordeaux after playing key role in Milan's humiliating 3-0 UEFA Cup exit to same club. Debut delayed until October because of knee operation. Big and strong in traditional centre-forward mould. Back-up to Weah.

Marco Simone, striker, 27. Complete centre-forward -- slick on turn with eye for opportunist goal -- but waited until this season to shake off reputation as super-sub and claim first-team place, at Roberto Baggio's expense. Off-the-field friendship with Weah has produced intuitive on-the-pitch partnership.

Roberto Baggio, striker, 29. Finally showing signs of best form since joining Milan from Juventus in 1995. Still set to start match on sub's bench. Despite limited appearances, last year pulled off rare feat of successive league titles with two teams: Juve and Milan. 24 goals in 44 internationals with Italy.
